title: Al-'Alaq 96:17-19 with words spaced, and the questions
subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
unit: Spring 2: Al-'Alaq 13 to 19, At-Tin and meem sakinah
source: Written for quran/y3 lesson 20 (Pupil PDF worksheet: Al-'Alaq 96:17-19 with words spaced, and the questions)
intro: Lesson 20. Read each word slowly, pointing with your finger. Only the Arabic is the Qur'an; the English is a translation of its meaning.

arabic.text: فَلْيَدْعُ نَادِيَهُۥ (١٧) سَنَدْعُ ٱلزَّبَانِيَةَ (١٨) كَلَّا لَا تُطِعْهُ وَٱسْجُدْ وَٱقْتَرِب ۩ (١٩)

head: Ayah
Translation of the meaning (Saheeh International)
rows: Then let him call his associates;
We will call the angels of Hell.
No! Do not obey him. But prostrate and draw near [to Allah].

head: Word
Where
Rule
How to read it
rows: Sukoon on ل, then a clear د and ع
Do not add a vowel to the laam
Light hum, tongue ready for د
Qalqalah: ق inside, ب at the stop
Small bounce on ق; bigger bounce on ب when stopping
A small bounce on the د

keywords.def: putting the forehead on the ground in prayer
a place in the Qur'an where we may prostrate

questions.q: Chunk and link Al-'Alaq 96:17-19 together, ayah by ayah.
questions.a: The class recites 96:17-19 together without the mushaf.

questions.q: Listening rota: today's group recites 96:17-19 to the teacher, one by one. Everyone else: 3-3-link the same ayat, then tick the revision log.
questions.a: Pupil recites with no help; the teacher marks hifdh and tajweed on the rubric and gives one target.

questions.q: Recite all of Al-'Alaq 96:1 to 19 to a partner. Partner ticks each ayah said with no help.
questions.a: 19 ticks; any slips are noted for home revision.

questions.q: Write one sentence: what is sujud at-tilawah and when might we make it?
questions.a: A prostration made when reciting or hearing an ayah of sajdah, such as 96:19.

options: prostrate and draw near to Allah
questions.a: A) prostrate and draw near to Allah. 96:19: 'Do not obey him. But prostrate and draw near.' Calling his associates was the disbeliever in 96:17.

questions.q: How many ayat are in Al-'Alaq?
Think again: Al-'Alaq ends: 'prostrate and draw near'. Why do you think sujud is the moment we are closest to Allah?
questions.a: In sujud we put our forehead on the ground for Allah alone: the most humble position, so the closest.
